dedupe_keys.name: cocorahs community collaborative rain hail and snow network observations

description: CoCoRaHS, the Community Collaborative Rain, Hail and Snow Network, is a non-profit network of volunteers who measure rain, hail and snow with low-cost standard gauges and report daily through its website. It began at the Colorado Climate Center at Colorado State University in 1998, after the 1997 Fort Collins flood, and now involves thousands of volunteers in the Northern Hemisphere, with NOAA and the National Science Foundation as major sponsors. Public report lists and maps give daily and multi-day precipitation, significant intense precipitation events, hail, condition monitoring (drought impacts) and evapotranspiration reports by station. The data are freely available to governments, researchers, business and the public under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 licence (site content under CC BY 4.0), with a request to acknowledge the source; the data are provided as is. The network says users include the National Weather Service, hydrologists, emergency managers, city water supply, conservation and stormwater utilities, and insurers. Caveats: observations are volunteer readings at uneven density, stations join and leave, and no bulk download was checked. Simulation uses: dense rainfall inputs for urban drainage and stormwater models, verification of radar rainfall in flash flood events, local drought impact evidence for water supply planning, and hail footprints. Related records: the NOAA National Water Model (model-noaa-national-water-model).
